title: 10 Triple Whale alternatives for ecommerce teams in 2026
summary: Compare 10 Triple Whale alternatives by attribution depth, pricing and tracking fit, with honest limits and criteria for choosing one in 2026.
body_markdown:
Your store switches dashboards after a month of ROAS figures that don't match the bank statement. The replacement shows a third set of numbers. Now the paid media lead, finance manager and analyst each have a different answer to the same question: did those campaigns make money?


**Start with the data problem, not the dashboard.** A new dashboard reads tags and connected data sources. It doesn't, by itself, verify that those tags work. Trackingplan covers that layer: it makes sure campaigns are optimized on conversion data the team can trust. It checks that purchases are counted once across Meta Pixel and CAPI, reconcile with GA4, and carry the right values, click IDs and UTMs before automated bidding learns from bad data.


Attribution adds another source of disagreement. Different models can assign different credit to the same purchase without either system having a broken tag.[GolfRep's guide to marketing attribution](https://www.golfrep.co/blogs/marketing-attribution-challenges) provides useful context for separating attribution questions from collection failures.


> A different revenue total isn't proof of better tracking. Ask which orders, hits and attribution rules explain the difference.


The **Triple Whale alternatives** below answer a different question: how should your store measure sales and spend? Some model channel contribution. Others calculate profit, organize business data or deliver conversion events. Read each entry with one test in mind: **does this tool fix the problem you have now?**


## 1. Trackingplan


Trackingplan, your digital analytics agent.


**Trackingplan fits teams that want to ask about their campaigns and trust the answer.** It's a digital analytics agent, trained to act as a digital analyst, and it works on any website or app, from a Shopify store to a SaaS product.


It reads spend, clicks, conversions and conversion value from connected ad accounts on eleven platforms, including Google Ads, Meta Ads, TikTok Ads and Amazon Ads, so every campaign has its ROAS. Then it sets those numbers against what your Meta Pixel, CAPI and GA4 actually receive. Ask which campaigns lost ROAS this week or where a purchase is counted twice, and it investigates before it answers, with the evidence behind each conclusion.


- **Campaign view:** ROAS per campaign from eleven ad platforms, next to the conversions your site sends.
- **Data checks:** the same purchase across Meta Pixel, CAPI and GA4, with its value, click IDs and UTMs, and gaps routed to whoever owns the tag.
- **Where you ask:** the app, Slack, or Claude, ChatGPT and Cursor. Reports run on demand, daily or weekly.


[Trackingplan](https://www.trackingplan.com/landings/paid-media) starts at **$99 per month** on the Starter plan, with a 9-day free trial and no credit card.


### Delivery still needs verification


[Meta's Conversions API best practices](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/ads-commerce/conversions-api/best-practices/) describe matching event names and event IDs for browser/server deduplication and evaluate Event Match Quality per event in Events Manager. A server-side integration therefore needs more than confirmation that requests were sent.


**The conversion-data test:** During the trial, ask it about a discrepancy you already know and check that the answer points to the orders and hits behind it.


## 2. Northbeam


Northbeam website


*Screenshot: Northbeam website.*


**Northbeam fits teams that need deeper cross-channel measurement, not just a different dashboard.** Its appeal is the ability to compare click-based attribution with view-through measurement and add modeling or experiments when the channel mix demands them.


[Northbeam](https://www.northbeam.io/) lists Starter at **$1,500 per month** and Professional at **$3,500 per month** . Confirm eligibility, contract terms and included capabilities before budgeting around those starting prices.


### Where the extra depth helps


Say paid social introduces a customer who later returns through branded search. A click-only report and a view-inclusive model may tell different stories about that purchase. Northbeam gives analysts more ways to examine that difference, including deterministic views on some plans.


- **Measurement coverage:** Multi-touch attribution, click and view-through measurement, plus optional media mix modeling and incrementality.
- **Platform fit:** Higher tiers support ecommerce requirements beyond a Shopify-centered reporting setup.
- **Buying trade-off:** Sales-led plans and possible annual terms require more commitment than a lightweight analytics app.


Use this[guide to marketing attribution tools](https://www.trackingplan.com/blog/marketing-attribution-tools-how-to-measure-campaign-roi-accurately) to distinguish the measurement method you need from the dashboard you prefer.


**The conversion-data test:** Ask the vendor to reconcile selected orders with the events and journeys behind them. More advanced attribution won't establish whether your purchase tag fired twice after a checkout release. I'd shortlist Northbeam when analysts will use its measurement depth, not when the immediate problem is unexplained missing purchases.


## 3. Rockerbox


Rockerbox website


*Screenshot: Rockerbox website.*


A store running digital ads alongside offline activity needs more than a ledger of tracked clicks. **Rockerbox suits a mature measurement program** where analysts compare customer paths, modeled channel contribution and experiment results.


[Rockerbox](https://www.rockerbox.com/) combines multi-touch attribution, media mix modeling and incrementality testing, with custom pricing available through the vendor. Its reporting can accommodate digital and offline channels rather than restricting analysis to standard ecommerce click paths.


That breadth is useful, but it changes the buying decision. Your team needs someone who can define the question, inspect the inputs and explain why different methods disagree.


> **Practical rule:** Don't buy a broader measurement platform unless someone owns the decisions its reports are supposed to support.


The advantage is methodological choice. Customer-path analysis can inform tactical investigation, while modeling and tests can address questions that click attribution alone can't settle. This explanation of[attribution bias](https://www.trackingplan.com/blog/attribution-bias-example) is useful when assessing whether your current reporting systematically favors particular channels.


**The trade-off is operational complexity.** Expect to define data sources, reporting requirements and measurement assumptions rather than treating implementation as a dashboard login.


For the demo, bring a known discrepancy and request a traceable explanation. Separate missing source events from differences caused by attribution rules. Rockerbox is a stronger fit for cross-channel measurement than for a store whose only unmet need is basic Shopify profit tracking.


## 4. Fospha


Fospha website


*Screenshot: Fospha website.*


**Fospha is relevant when last-click reporting gives you an incomplete view of paid social, video and awareness activity.** It focuses on full-funnel ecommerce measurement, including impressions and views rather than clicks alone.


[Fospha](https://www.fospha.com/) combines channel data with sales information and can include destinations such as Amazon and TikTok Shop; its product guidance describes a **daily measurement cadence** . Request a quote rather than assuming a public entry price.


### Model contribution without confusing it with event proof


A brand may advertise on social, then receive purchases through its website and marketplaces. Fospha's blended measurement perspective can help assess that activity without accepting every ad platform's conversion claims at face value.


That's a different job from verifying the purchase hit. A modeled channel contribution isn't a direct click-to-order ledger, and analysts need to be comfortable explaining that distinction to finance.


- **Strong fit:** Ecommerce teams evaluating impression-driven channels and sales beyond their own checkout.
- **Useful complement:** A broader measurement view alongside tactical reporting inside ad platforms.
- **Main limitation:** Modeling doesn't replace checks for missing events, duplicate purchases or incorrect values.


This[practical guide to marketing mix modeling](https://www.trackingplan.com/blog/marketing-mix-modeling-a-practical-guide-for-analysts-en) helps frame questions about inputs and interpretation.


**The conversion-data test:** Establish how sales, refunds and channel feeds enter the model. Then investigate event-delivery failures separately. Choose Fospha to improve how you assess contribution, not to diagnose a broken dataLayer after a release.


## 5. Polar Analytics


Polar Analytics website


*Screenshot: Polar Analytics website.*


Your analyst exports store orders, joins advertising spend and rebuilds the same business report each week. **Polar Analytics addresses that reporting and data-access problem** , with attribution inside a wider ecommerce analytics platform.


[Polar Analytics](https://www.polaranalytics.com/) offers dashboards, custom reports, a dedicated Snowflake database and an ecommerce semantic layer. Its Core and Custom plan information doesn't provide a clear public price, so evaluate the proposed package rather than an assumed entry cost.


The database matters when analysts need to investigate definitions instead of accepting dashboard totals. However, warehouse access doesn't automatically establish that the events loaded into it are complete.


### Buy the analytics layer you'll actually use


- **Business reporting:** Combine commerce and marketing analysis rather than maintaining separate reporting workflows.
- **Operational features:** Assess alerts and scheduled reports against the team's reporting needs.
- **Optional capabilities:** Confirm incrementality testing, data activations and advertising signals in the proposed scope.


**The trade-off is platform breadth.** Polar may be excessive if your only requirement is campaign attribution. It becomes more relevant when the same team also owns executive reporting and business analysis.


For the conversion-data test, request an order-level reconciliation using your definitions for revenue, refunds, tax and shipping. Confirm which access permissions and refresh options come with the contract. A flexible reporting layer is valuable only if your analyst can inspect the discrepancy rather than reproduce it in another chart.


## 6. ThoughtMetric


ThoughtMetric website


*Screenshot: ThoughtMetric website.*


**ThoughtMetric is a more focused choice for ecommerce attribution.** It connects campaigns, products and customer journeys without requiring the same broad measurement program as an enterprise modeling platform.


[ThoughtMetric](https://thoughtmetric.io/) publishes pricing starting at **$99 per month for up to 50,000 monthly pageviews** , with costs scaling by usage. Check current terms against actual store traffic, especially when browsing volume grows faster than orders.


Its attribution models include first-touch, last-touch, linear paid, position-based and multi-touch. Product information also describes server-side tracking, Meta and Google Conversions API integrations, and support for Shopify, WooCommerce, Magento and BigCommerce.


- **What works:** Product-level reporting helps analysts connect campaign credit with the items customers buy.
- **What to watch:** Pageview-based pricing can change the economics for a high-traffic store.
- **What it doesn't prove:** Attribution estimates don't establish that advertising caused the purchase.


The server-side integrations deserve a technical review, not just a tick in the feature matrix. Ask which system generates the event ID, how retries work and whether browser and server events use consistent values.


**My recommendation:** Shortlist ThoughtMetric when you want understandable ecommerce attribution and visible entry pricing. Compare its attributed purchases with backend orders before relying on campaign totals. If you need media mix modeling or an enterprise incrementality program, assess that requirement separately rather than expecting a focused attribution tool to cover it.


## 7. Wicked Reports


Wicked Reports website


*Screenshot: Wicked Reports website.*


A subscription customer's initial order doesn't describe the full value of acquisition. **Wicked Reports focuses on longer customer journeys, cohorts and lifetime value** , making it relevant when repeat purchases or delayed conversions affect your decisions.


[Wicked Reports](https://www.wickedreports.com/) publishes starting monthly prices of **$499 for Measure, $699 for Scale, $999 for Maximize and $4,999 for Enterprise** , with pricing tied to annual revenue bands. Confirm which band and capabilities apply to your business.


### Evaluate customer value, not just the checkout


FunnelVision reporting views, lifetime lookback and lookforward, and integrations with ad platforms, carts and CRMs support analysis beyond the first sale. That can help a retention-heavy brand distinguish immediate acquisition performance from later customer revenue.


The main trade-offs are cost and feature packaging. Capabilities such as Meta CAPI and Amazon revenue integration depend on higher plans or paid additions, so don't assume every quoted package includes them.


> Longer attribution windows can reveal repeat revenue. They can't prove that an old ad caused every later purchase.


**The conversion-data test:** Trace a customer from acquisition through repeat orders, refunds and subscription changes. Inspect how the platform joins customer records and classifies subsequent revenue.


Wicked Reports is worth assessing when customer value over time is the missing view. It's harder to justify when a smaller store needs only a basic profit report or when the problem is duplicate purchase events reaching an ad platform.


## 8. TrueProfit


TrueProfit website


*Screenshot: TrueProfit website.*


**TrueProfit answers a financial question before an attribution question.** If the team can see sales and ad spend but can't explain what remains after costs, a profit-focused tool may be a better purchase than deeper channel modeling.


[TrueProfit](https://trueprofit.io/) lists monthly prices of **$35 for Basic, $60 for Advanced, $100 for Ultimate and $200 for Enterprise** . Check order limits, extra-order charges and current trial terms when calculating the total cost.


The platform combines profit-and-loss reporting and cost tracking with customer lifetime value and product analytics. It also offers store-level views for multiple Shopify stores, while marketing attribution is available on Ultimate and Enterprise.


- **Best use:** Bring product costs, expenses and advertising spend into the same profit analysis.
- **Plan constraint:** Entry pricing doesn't include every attribution capability.
- **Measurement limit:** Profit reporting doesn't replace full-funnel measurement or media mix modeling.


### Validate the costs behind the margin


Say a product's advertising performance looks strong, but returns and fulfillment costs leave little contribution. TrueProfit's category is better suited to that investigation than a tool bought mainly to redistribute conversion credit.


Your acceptance test should include refunded orders, shipping costs, payment fees and product cost changes. Then inspect the ad-spend imports and currency treatment.


**The trade-off:** You gain a clearer financial view, not automatic proof that Meta Pixel, CAPI and GA4 received the correct purchase. Keep profit reconciliation and event QA as separate tasks.


## 9. BeProfit


BeProfit website


*Screenshot: BeProfit website.*


Start with the report the finance lead needs. If it's order profitability, expenses and product performance, **BeProfit belongs on the shortlist** . It's less appropriate when the primary requirement is advanced cross-channel attribution.


[BeProfit](https://www.beprofit.ai/) lists a free plan and monthly prices of **$29 for Basic, $99 for Pro, $149 for Scale and from $249 for Enterprise** , with features, order limits and historical coverage varying by plan.


Its profit dashboard and expense tracking provide the core value. Marketing analytics start on Scale, while UTM attribution and lifetime-value cohorts sit on higher plans. Multi-store support is listed for Enterprise, so agencies should confirm the proposed account structure.


### UTM attribution still depends on clean UTMs


A report can group campaign revenue only as consistently as the campaign identifiers it receives. If email, paid social and affiliates use conflicting naming conventions, the analyst still needs to resolve those inputs.


- **Useful strength:** Order and product analysis keeps the discussion focused on profit rather than platform-reported ROAS alone.
- **Buying caution:** Match the required history, order volume and cohort features to the actual plan.
- **Category boundary:** Don't expect a profit platform to replace incrementality testing or media mix modeling.


For the conversion-data test, inspect a campaign journey through checkout and compare its UTM classification with the order record. Then validate expense handling separately. BeProfit can clarify whether the store made money without resolving every reason the ad platforms disagree.


## 10. HYROS


HYROS website


*Screenshot: HYROS website.*


**HYROS deserves attention when revenue doesn't end at a standard online checkout.** Phone sales, recurring payments and high-ticket funnels introduce different attribution requirements from a straightforward product purchase.


[HYROS](https://hyros.com/) covers ecommerce, SaaS, B2B calls and education-related sales models. Current pricing and plan requirements need a vendor quote rather than an assumed public rate.


For an ecommerce team, the important question is whether that broader scope matches the actual sales process. A complex funnel benefits from revenue attribution only when lead records, calls and completed sales can be connected reliably.


### Inspect the handoff to offline outcomes


Google's[offline conversion workflow](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/7012522) uses the GCLID to connect an ad click with a later outcome and distinguishes primary, biddable conversion actions from secondary, observation-only actions. That makes identifier capture and action classification useful acceptance tests for any longer-journey setup.


- **Potential fit:** Businesses that need call or funnel attribution alongside ecommerce revenue.
- **Required validation:** Confirm the specific CRM, call, checkout and recurring-revenue integrations.
- **Separate requirement:** Dedicated profit reporting and data-quality monitoring still need their own evaluation.


Ask for a walkthrough from click to lead, lead to sale and sale to imported conversion. Don't settle for a revenue chart without evidence of the joins.


HYROS is a less direct fit when your checkout journey is simple and your missing capability is a store P&L. Broader sales-model coverage isn't valuable unless your team needs it.

The split matters. Trackingplan sits upstream of the report: it checks what reaches Meta CAPI, GA4 and the dataLayer before revenue is attributed, and sets it against the ROAS each platform reports. Northbeam, Rockerbox, Fospha, Polar Analytics, ThoughtMetric, Wicked Reports and HYROS mainly change how clicks, views, calls and orders are assigned. TrueProfit and BeProfit then push assigned revenue toward costs, margin and cohorts.


If the purchase hit is unreliable, an attribution tier will repackage the gap. If totals reconcile but margin is missing, tag infrastructure will not show contribution by product, channel or cohort.


## Pick the tool that fixes your problem first


**Sort the problem before the vendor.** A cleaner dashboard only helps if the conversion inputs behind it are sound. When numbers disagree, inspect hits, dataLayer events, Meta Pixel and CAPI deduplication, click IDs and attribution windows before comparing feature lists. Align revenue definitions and time zones too. A bank deposit, backend order total and attributed revenue report don't measure the same thing.


Match the tool to the missing capability. TrueProfit and BeProfit emphasize profit. Wicked Reports emphasizes customer value over longer journeys. Northbeam, Rockerbox and Fospha address broader measurement questions, while Polar Analytics adds a business-data layer. Attribution and profit tools answer reporting questions. Tag-level infrastructure answers a different question: whether the event stream feeding those reports is complete and consistent. Confirm plan limits, order caps, historical coverage and integrations in writing before you commit.


### Make the trial answer an operational question


Choose one known discrepancy and follow it through the proposed setup. Preserve the order record, tracking hit, dataLayer state and destination response. For consent, inspect websites and server-side behavior before and after the user changes their choice.[Google's Consent Mode configuration guidance](https://support.google.com/tagmanager/answer/14565698) supports regional defaults and overrides, so test the markets you serve rather than checking only whether a banner appears. Give the privacy lead evidence of tag behavior, not just a screenshot of the CMP.


For offline sales, check delivery schedules and bidding settings as carefully as reporting totals.[Google Ads recommends uploading offline conversions at least daily](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/10029210) , including values for relevant value-based bidding strategies. A conversion visible in a report may still be doing nothing for bidding.


Agencies should compare **recurring human work** , not subscription cost alone. Establish who investigates an exception, who owns the tag and what evidence reaches the client. If phone sales are part of the account,[Bluelight's call tracking comparison](https://www.bluelightads.com/call-tracking-software) can help frame that separate requirement.


> **Buying test:** Ask the team to explain a discrepancy from the underlying evidence before accepting a cleaner dashboard as an improvement.


In Trackingplan, scheduled tasks run daily or weekly, and each task uses one credit. One credit costs 1€. Findings route to the responsible team with links to the underlying hits.


Keep the final decision narrow. Buy the missing capability, retain the reporting that works and verify every event, property and value on real traffic throughout the change.
